components.text:
Assumptions: Standard working hours are 9:00 AM to 5:30 PM for all locations. On November 5, 2024, the UK is on GMT and the US is on Standard Time (EST/PST) as Daylight Saving Time ends on November 3 in the US.

Timezone Offsets:
- London (GMT): UTC+0
- New York (EST): UTC-5
- San Francisco (PST): UTC-8

Available 45-Minute Slots:
There are NO 45-minute slots where all participants are within 9:00 AM to 5:30 PM. The maximum overlap between all three locations is only 30 minutes.

Best Partial Overlap (30 minutes):
- London: 5:00 PM - 5:30 PM GMT
- New York: 12:00 PM - 12:30 PM EST
- San Francisco: 9:00 AM - 9:30 AM PST

Recommended Alternative (Requires 15-min extension for London):
- Slot 1: 5:00 PM - 5:45 PM GMT | 12:00 PM - 12:45 PM EST | 9:00 AM - 9:45 AM PST
- Slot 2: 4:45 PM - 5:30 PM GMT | 11:45 AM - 12:30 PM EST | 8:45 AM - 9:30 AM PST (SF starts 15 mins early)

Quick Actions:
- [Button: Open World Clock] https://www.timeanddate.com/worldclock/

components.text:
Nutritional Comparison (per 100g serving)

Nutrient | Raw Atlantic Salmon | Grilled Chicken Breast | Firm Tofu
Calories | 208 kcal | 165 kcal | 83 kcal
Protein | 20g | 31g | 10g
Total Fat | 13g | 3.6g | 5g
Vitamin B12 | 3.2 mcg | 0.3 mcg | 0 mcg (unless fortified)

Recommendation:
For a high-protein, low-fat diet with a concern for B12, Grilled Chicken Breast is the best option for protein density and low fat. However, Salmon is the only significant source of B12 among the three. If B12 is the priority, Salmon is superior despite the higher fat content (which consists of healthy Omega-3s). If strictly adhering to low-fat, choose Chicken and supplement B12 or ensure Tofu is fortified.

Icons:
- Health: https://img.icons8.com/ios/50/heart-health.png
- Protein: https://img.icons8.com/ios/50/flex-biceps.png

Sources:
- https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/

components.text:
Cyberpunk as a genre is defined by the juxtaposition of advanced technological achievement and social decay. This list highlights foundational films that established the aesthetic of neon-lit rain, corporate dominance, and underground rebellion.

Assumptions: Classic status is based on cultural impact and genre-defining tropes.
Ridley Scott | High Tech: Bio-engineered Replicants / Low Life: Gritty, overpopulated Los Angeles.
Katsuhiro Otomo | High Tech: Secret government psychic experiments / Low Life: Biker gangs in a post-apocalyptic Neo-Tokyo.
Mamoru Oshii | High Tech: Cybernetic bodies and brain-hacking / Low Life: Urban alienation and political corruption.
Kathryn Bigelow | High Tech: SQUID devices recording human memories / Low Life: Social unrest and black-market data dealing.
The Wachowskis | High Tech: A sophisticated AI simulation / Low Life: Humanity living in the subterranean ruins of Zion.

components.text: This guide provides a structured approach to discussing F. Scott Fitzgerald's masterpiece, focusing on the decay of the American Dream and the power of symbols.

Set in the summer of 1922, the story follows Nick Carraway, who moves to Long Island and becomes entangled in the life of his mysterious neighbor, Jay Gatsby. Gatsby is a self-made millionaire obsessed with reuniting with his former flame, Daisy Buchanan, who is married to the wealthy but unfaithful Tom. As Gatsby uses his lavish parties to draw Daisy in, the facade of his wealth and the purity of his dream begin to crumble. The narrative explores themes of social stratification and the moral void of the Jazz Age, culminating in a series of tragic events that reveal the hollowness of the upper class and the impossibility of recapturing the past.
How does Gatsby’s pursuit of the American Dream differ from the reality of the social class he tries to join?
What does the 'Green Light' at the end of Daisy’s dock represent at the beginning versus the end of the novel?
Analyze the Valley of Ashes: How does it serve as a symbolic contrast to East and West Egg?
Do any characters in the book truly achieve 'The American Dream', or is it depicted as an inherent illusion?
How does the recurring motif of 'The Eyes of Doctor T.J. Eckleburg' function as a commentary on the characters' morality?
Rhapsody in Blue by George Gershwin (1924)
West End Blues by Louis Armstrong (1928)
The Charleston by James P. Johnson (1923)

Zen Rock | $150 | Rock | Low (Mt. Fuji - 2.5 hours)

Summary
The 2022 MacBook Air (M2) introduced a redesigned chassis, a slightly larger and brighter Liquid Retina display, and the upgraded M2 silicon, while the 2020 model (M1) remains a benchmark for value and efficiency in the classic wedge-shaped design.

Model | Base CPU Cores | Base GPU Cores | Max Unified Memory | Weight (lbs)
--- | --- | --- | --- | ---

- Display: The M2 model features a 13.6-inch Liquid Retina display with 500 nits brightness, compared to the M1's 13.3-inch Retina display at 400 nits.
- Charging: The M2 model reintroduced the MagSafe 3 charging port, freeing up both Thunderbolt ports during use.
- Camera: The M2 features a 1080p FaceTime HD camera, an upgrade over the 720p sensor in the M1.

Quick Actions:

components.text:
Summary
The primary difference lies in the environment they are designed to withstand. 3-season tents prioritize ventilation and weight savings for spring, summer, and fall, while 4-season tents (winter tents) are built to endure heavy snow and high winds.

Structural Comparison
Feature | 3-Season Tent | 4-Season Tent
--- | --- | ---
Pole Material/Thickness | Thinner aluminum (8.5mm - 9mm); focus on flexibility. | Thicker, high-grade aluminum (9.5mm+); more intersection points for rigidity.
Canopy Mesh % | High mesh percentage (50-70%) for airflow and weight reduction. | Minimal mesh; mostly solid fabric (nylon/polyester) to retain heat and block spindrift.
Snow Load Capacity | Low; steep walls and mesh can sag or collapse under heavy snow. | High; rounded dome shapes and sturdy frames shed snow and support weight.

Scottish Highlands Recommendation (July)
Recommendation: 3-Season Tent
Reasoning: July in the Highlands is characterized by rain and strong winds, but not heavy snow. A 3-season tent offers the necessary ventilation to combat condensation and is significantly lighter for long treks. However, ensure the tent has a sturdy "semi-geodesic" or "tunnel" design, as Highland winds can be severe even in summer.

Essential Gear for Scotland July
- Sturdy tent stakes (for boggy or rocky ground).
- High-quality rain fly with a high hydrostatic head rating.
- Bug mesh (essential for protection against the infamous Highland midges).

Icons:
- Camping: https://img.icons8.com/ios/50/camping-tent.png
- Weather: https://img.icons8.com/ios/50/mountain.png

components.text:
Assumptions: This framework assumes a primary goal of maximizing value for a high-frequency traveler to Japan who prioritizes comfort and cost-offsetting.

Travel Credit Card Evaluation Framework (5-Point)

1. No Foreign Transaction Fees (Weight: 30%)
Essential for Japan, where many local shops and restaurants are cash-heavy or use local payment processors. Saving 3% on every transaction outside the US is a guaranteed return.

2. Point Multipliers on Dining (Weight: 25%)
With a $2,000 monthly spend on travel/dining, a 3x or 4x multiplier translates to 72,000 - 96,000 points annually. In Tokyo, a food mecca, this is where you will accumulate the most rewards.

3. Annual Fee vs. Credits (Weight: 20%)
Evaluate if the "effective cost" is low. If a $550 card offers $300 in travel credits and $200 in dining credits, the $50 net cost is easily justified by the other perks.

4. Lounge Access (Weight: 15%)
Important for the long-haul flight to Tokyo (approx. 11-14 hours from the US). Access to Priority Pass or carrier-specific lounges (like JAL/ANA partners) significantly improves the transit experience.

5. Global Entry / TSA PreCheck Credit (Weight: 10%)
A standard perk that saves $100 every 4-5 years. While useful, it is a one-time benefit and shouldn't be the primary driver of the card choice.

Recommended Weighting for $2,000 Monthly Spend
Given your high dining and travel spend, you should prioritize Point Multipliers and No Foreign Transaction Fees. A card with 4x on dining will yield enough points for a free round-trip flight to Japan within 12-18 months of regular spending.

Verification Steps for 2025
1. Check current sign-up bonuses (SUBs) which fluctuate monthly.
2. Confirm if the card's transfer partners include ANA or Japan Airlines for maximum point value.
3. Verify if the lounge network (e.g., Centurion vs. Priority Pass) has good coverage at Haneda (HND) or Narita (NRT).

Example Cards for 2025 (Synthetic/Plausible)
- Option 1: The Global Voyager | 4x Dining/Travel | $0 Foreign Fee | $250 Annual Fee
- Option 2: Elite Transit Card | 3x Dining | Lounge Access | $595 Annual Fee
- Option 3: Simple Traveler | 2x Everything | No Fee | $95 Annual Fee

          id: text_1
          text: "Assumptions: This framework assumes a primary goal of maximizing value for a high-frequency traveler to Japan who prioritizes comfort and cost-offsetting.

Travel Credit Card Evaluation Framework (5-Point)

1. No Foreign Transaction Fees (Weight: 30%)
Essential for Japan, where many local shops and restaurants are cash-heavy or use local payment processors. Saving 3% on every transaction outside the US is a guaranteed return.

2. Point Multipliers on Dining (Weight: 25%)
With a $2,000 monthly spend on travel/dining, a 3x or 4x multiplier translates to 72,000 - 96,000 points annually. In Tokyo, a food mecca, this is where you will accumulate the most rewards.

3. Annual Fee vs. Credits (Weight: 20%)
Evaluate if the "effective cost" is low. If a $550 card offers $300 in travel credits and $200 in dining credits, the $50 net cost is easily justified by the other perks.

4. Lounge Access (Weight: 15%)
Important for the long-haul flight to Tokyo (approx. 11-14 hours from the US). Access to Priority Pass or carrier-specific lounges (like JAL/ANA partners) significantly improves the transit experience.

5. Global Entry / TSA PreCheck Credit (Weight: 10%)
A standard perk that saves $100 every 4-5 years. While useful, it is a one-time benefit and shouldn't be the primary driver of the card choice.

Recommended Weighting for $2,000 Monthly Spend
Given your high dining and travel spend, you should prioritize Point Multipliers and No Foreign Transaction Fees. A card with 4x on dining will yield enough points for a free round-trip flight to Japan within 12-18 months of regular spending.

Verification Steps for 2025
1. Check current sign-up bonuses (SUBs) which fluctuate monthly.
2. Confirm if the card's transfer partners include ANA or Japan Airlines for maximum point value.
3. Verify if the lounge network (e.g., Centurion vs. Priority Pass) has good coverage at Haneda (HND) or Narita (NRT).

Example Cards for 2025 (Synthetic/Plausible)
- Option 1: The Global Voyager | 4x Dining/Travel | $0 Foreign Fee | $250 Annual Fee
- Option 2: Elite Transit Card | 3x Dining | Lounge Access | $595 Annual Fee
- Option 3: Simple Traveler | 2x Everything | No Fee | $95 Annual Fee

Summary
The Herman Miller Aeron is a classic mesh task chair focused on suspended support, while the Steelcase Gesture is designed for modern tech users, supporting a wide range of postures and device-usage styles.

Ergonomic Feature Comparison

Lumbar Support
- Aeron (Size B): Features the PostureFit SL system. It uses two adjustable pads that stabilize the sacrum and support the lumbar region of the spine to mimic a standing posture.
- Gesture: Features "3D LiveBack" technology. The backrest automatically contours to mimic the natural movement of the spine, providing continuous support as you change positions.

Armrest Movement
- Aeron (Size B): 3D Armrests. They adjust for height, depth (sliding forward/backward), and pivot (turning inward/outward). They are attached to the seat back.
- Gesture: 4D Armrests. Known for the best range in the industry, they adjust for height, width, depth, and 360-degree pivot. They are designed to support users holding mobile devices or tablets.

Tilt Options
- Aeron (Size B): Standard model includes a Tilt Limiter with three settings (upright, mid-recline, full recline) and a Seat Angle adjustment (Forward Tilt) for engaged tasks.
- Gesture: Features a variable back stop with four positions. It lacks the forward tilt option found on the Aeron but offers a more seamless "synchro-tilt" that keeps feet flat on the floor while reclining.

Summary
Garmin Venu 2 is a fitness-first watch with deep physiological data, while the Apple Watch Series 8 is a general-purpose smartwatch with advanced medical-grade health sensors.

Sensor Comparison

Pulse Ox (SpO2) Monitoring
- Garmin Venu 2: Offers "All-Day" and "Sleep-Only" tracking. It provides a continuous graph of blood oxygen saturation, though it is heavy on battery usage.
- Apple Watch Series 8: Performs periodic background checks and allows for on-demand manual readings. It is highly integrated into the Health app for spotting long-term trends.

Sleep Stage Tracking
- Garmin Venu 2: Uses heart rate, heart rate variability (HRV), and movement to identify Light, Deep, and REM stages. It provides a "Sleep Score" based on quality.
- Apple Watch Series 8: Uses a machine-learning model to identify REM, Core, and Deep sleep. It is widely considered one of the most accurate wrist-based trackers for stage transitions.

Heart Rate Sampling Frequency
- Garmin Venu 2: Samples heart rate continuously (every second), both at rest and during exercise. This provides a very high-resolution view of heart rate changes.
- Apple Watch Series 8: During rest, it samples every few minutes to save battery. During exercise, it switches to continuous (every second) sampling.

Comparison Table
Feature | Garmin Venu 2 | Apple Watch Series 8
--- | --- | ---
Resting HR Sampling | Every 1 second | Every 1-5 minutes
Exercise HR Sampling | Every 1 second | Every 1 second
SpO2 Accuracy | High (Consumer grade) | High (FDA cleared in some regions)
Battery Life | Up to 11 days | Up to 18 hours

Sources:
- https://www.garmin.com/en-US/p/707538
- https://support.apple.com/kb/SP878

components.text: Pruning Shears Guide for Seattle Rose Gardens
Bypass Pruners: These work like scissors, where two sharp blades pass by each other. This creates a clean, precise cut.
Anvil Pruners: These have one sharp blade that closes down onto a flat metal or plastic plate (the anvil). This works like a knife on a chopping board.
Roses have live green tissue that needs to heal quickly to prevent disease (common in damp Seattle climates). Bypass shears provide a clean slice that leaves the plant's vascular system intact.
Why Anvil Shears Damage Live Tissue

Anvil shears use a crushing motion to complete the cut. On live green stems, this crushing action bruises the delicate cambium layer and mashes the stem fibers. This creates a ragged wound that is slow to heal and serves as an entry point for fungi and pests. Anvil shears should only be used for dead, brittle wood where the crushing doesn't matter.
Prune in late February or early March when the forsythia blooms.
Always cut at a 45-degree angle, 1/4 inch above an outward-facing bud.
Clean your blades with isopropyl alcohol between plants to prevent the spread of Black Spot or Mildew.
